newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia criticises Russia, peacekeeping row grows.
newsitem.headline: Georgia criticises Russia, peacekeeping row grows.

text.p: The speaker of the Georgian parliament, stepping into a row with Moscow over Russia's peacekeeping troops in the former Soviet republic, accused President Boris Yeltsin's spokesman of "blackmail" on Wednesday.

Zurab Zhvania complained Russia had failed to respond to calls from Georgia and other ex-Soviet states that it step up the activities of its 2,500 troops guarding a buffer zone around Georgia's Black Sea province of Abkhazia, where separatist fighters drove out the Georgian army in 1993.

The Georgian parliament passed a resolution last week that Russia should withdraw its troops at the end of their current mandate on August 1 if they did not extend their patrols and begin helping Georgian refugees to resettle in Abkhazia.
Zhvania forecast that any departure of the peacekeepers would risk a flare-up in the conflict. "There are forces in Abkhazia interested in renewing the war," he said.

But he told a news conference that reported comments by Yeltsin's spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky on Monday -- that the Georgian parliament was trying to "blackmail" Moscow -- were in themselves akin to extortion.
"I consider this statement is blackmail itself," he said.
Yastrzhembsky said the Georgian parliament was "forcing us to rethink the advisability of the further presence of Russian peacekeepers in the conflict zone".
Analysts say their departure could spark a renewal of fighting between the separatists and Georgian government forces. Nearly four years of peace talks have reached a dead end.
Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze, the former Soviet foreign minister, last week offered a new start to negotiations but ruled out any recognition of Abkhazia's independence.
He also warned the separatists that they would be destroyed if they chose to go to war again with a rebuilt Georgian army.
Zhvania on Wednesday echoed Shevardnadze in saying new fighting would be "suicide" for the Abkhaz.
On Monday, a Russian army officer of the peacekeeping force was killed and two other servicemen were badly wounded when their armoured car hit a mine in the Abkhazian buffer zone.
Abkhaz officials, as they have after similar incidents in the past, blamed Georgian saboteurs. Georgia denied it.
Russian news agencies said a new round of talks between Abkhazia and Russia would start on Wednesday in Moscow.
